prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and its Z2 topological invariant, and the experimental observation of helical edge transport in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B039 as a single-part prize. Kane and Mele identified a new way to classify electronic matter, a Z2 invariant protected by time-reversal symmetry, together with a concrete physical consequence, helical edge states without any magnetic field. Molenkamp's group then observed the edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells, which required growth and device quality that few laboratories could provide. Nearly two decades of transport, imaging and spectroscopic work in several material families have left the interpretation stable. The concept has moved into photonics, cold atoms and acoustics. The chair asked what is new relative to 2016. My sentence is this: the 2016 prize concerned topological phase transitions and quantised Hall conductance in systems where time-reversal symmetry is broken, while the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 invariant describe a topological insulating state that exists with time-reversal symmetry intact and has no integer Hall conductance. This is a different state and a different invariant, so I regard it as an extension and not a repeat. After round 1 I narrow my own wording: the citation should be about the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 invariant and its observation, and should not claim topological insulators in general.
statement.case_against: The credit remains the main weakness, and no discussion in round 1 has repaired it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe prediction that directly guided Molenkamp's experiment, and the 3D topological-insulator work (Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, Hasan's group) lies outside the three names. A scoped citation makes the omission visible instead of hiding it, and it will still look incomplete to part of the community. The 2016 overlap is a second reservation, and applications are limited, so the case rests on conceptual and experimental impact. The three-person ceiling is also what prevents a fairer credit on this candidate. I accept that these costs are real and that I cannot remove them with the supplied names.

responses.point: Kroll holds that the lattice clock is a singular invention with a defined measurable result, that the 2016 prize weakens the novelty of a further topology prize, and that the lattice clock concept is not covered by any earlier prize.
responses.response: I accept that the magic-wavelength idea is distinct from the comb, and I was too quick to call it a refinement. I still weigh the two cases differently. The lattice clock is an outstanding measurement achievement, but its largest consequence, a redefinition of the second, has not happened, and its main scientific payoff is reaching smaller uncertainties for a known kind of measurement. The quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new organising principle for electronic matter. On 2016, the quantum Hall systems recognised then break time-reversal symmetry and carry an integer Hall conductance, while the spin Hall state has neither, so the novelty is substantive. You called B039's reach into other fields the strongest argument against your ranking, and I take that as a real concession. We still differ on weighting, and I do not move.

responses.point: Lindroth separates the lattice clock from the comb (counting cycles versus interrogating many neutral atoms without perturbation) and says the pending redefinition is a timing caution, not a flaw, while saying she does not want to mistake strong opening support for B039 for a weaker case for it.
responses.response: The distinction you draw between counting optical cycles and interrogating many atoms at once is a good one, and it persuades me that B022 is a distinct achievement. I also agree that opening support should not be read as merit, and that is why I give scientific reasons for B039 and not first-place counts. B022 stays my first alternative. My remaining reservation is the credit around it that you mention: other lattice-clock and ion-clock groups are outside the pair, so even the cleaner allocation is not complete. The B022 and B039 attribution problems differ in kind. For B022 the unnamed groups improved on a proposed and demonstrated concept, while for B039 an unnamed theory prediction directly guided the credited experiment. I think the second is the more serious problem, and I still prefer B039 because the new principle outweighs it.

responses.point: Danielsson says he would want the committee to settle whether the citation is for the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or for topological insulators broadly before relaxing his reservation, and notes that Zhang died in 2018 while Bernevig and Hughes are living.
responses.response: I agree and I commit to the 2D scope. The citation I propose names the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant, and the observation of helical edge transport in HgTe wells, and says nothing about 3D topological insulators. That meets your condition at least partly. Your point about Zhang's death is correct but I do not think it settles anything: the Nobel statute allows only living laureates, yet Bernevig and Hughes are alive, and the omission is a real choice that the committee should state openly in its own deliberation and not count as moot. I cannot say it is resolved. On B003, I share the concern about one name for a collaboration-scale discovery, and I would not support a two-part prize in which that is the second part.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, asks in the summary whether any defensible multi-name credit for B003 exists within the supplied names, and whether there is support for a two-part configuration under the three-laureate limit.
responses.response: On B003, I see no multi-name credit inside the supplied names, and I would not want to improvise one, since that is exactly the priority question the supplied file cannot settle. On the two-part question, I do not support B039 with B022, because the three-name B039 credit already uses the whole limit and a second part would force me to drop Mele or Molenkamp, which would damage the strongest feature of B039, the theory-to-experiment chain. I would not split the topological field either. A single-part prize is the cleanest outcome.

responses.point: Olsson, who moved to B039 after reading the opening ballots, argues that the Molenkamp credit is a real experimental contribution (atomic-precision quantum-well growth and characterisation) and not a decoration on a theory prize, and says she relies on recollection for the priority history.
responses.response: I agree that Molenkamp's part is essential and I would say so in the citation, which is why the experimental observation sits inside the wording. On the chair's question about recollection, I treat as settled that Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state, and that Molenkamp's group observed the helical edge conduction. I treat as open the exact priority and degree of influence of the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, and the 3D priority history. I have not verified those from the nominations, and they are the points that I would want the committee to check before the final vote.

uncertainties: Whether a 2D-scoped citation is enough to acknowledge the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction and the 3D work without seeming to dismiss them, since no wording can fully repair the omitted credit.
Whether the committee will accept the distinction from the 2016 prize (time-reversal symmetry intact, no integer Hall conductance) as sufficient.
The detailed priority history for BHZ and the 3D discoverers rests on my recollection and I have not verified it.
How much weight the committee should give to the pending redefinition of the second when comparing B022 with B039.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal ground has appeared for B039, B022 or B035. My research on turbulence, stochastic processes, random matrices and neural networks is not close to any shortlisted candidate, and none of the credited names is among my documented co-authors or supervisors. My position is unchanged from round 1 in the preferred configuration; I have only narrowed the citation wording.
